title: Counterpoint, New Orleans ragtime bands, Jack Laine's potato men, and Piron's music
summary: La Rocca says his counterpoint came from opera, lists the Bohler, Detroit and Shimmer bands and Tom Brown, and ridicules Jack Laine's paraders. He says Piron sent him music including Sister Kate, which he arranged.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: which became counterpoint in my case. If you listen to Livestable Blues, you'll see what I mean. Take each instrument alone and you've got three melodies in there. That's what old timers call a fugue. We didn't know what to call it. We didn't call it anything until they named it for us in Chicago. We didn't know what it was. We played it. That's all. Now, there was a sound. The father of this Detroit, Johnny Detroit's father had a band, a very good band. There was Mr. Bowler who had a band. Mr. who? Bowler. B-O-H-L-E-R. There was this fellow. I don't mean shoving them. They had ragtime bands. There was Johnny Shimmer.
Shimmer Manor had a band. Who? Shimmer Manor.

Yeah. Or Shimmer Manor. Shimmer Manor's band. They were all playing by notes. And they played in the carnival parades. Jack Lane played in the carnival parades. He hired some men who played by music. And he had some fakers in his band. And he also had some men who didn't play at all. Which they were called potato men. When you ask Jack Lane, when you go there, ask him about the potato men. How he made his money on unfortunate men. He had seven men playing. He played a bass drum. I'd be built and blowing my guts out on the carnival. And he had his son with a potato and an alto horn blowing to the ground blowing the dust off the floor. No music was coming out. He got paid for the parade. Then he'd have one or two other boys that was hangers on. There'd be seven men playing. There should have been ten playing. That's the kind of music he put out. He didn't look for music. He didn't know music. He wasn't even a musician. Yet, this man has believed in many things. That is the kind of people they give cupster at the jazz club. Then they had Tom Brown's band. It was a ragtime band. These boys went to Chicago before I did. I want to tell the truth about everything because if I tell you that I went before them, someone else before. But before these boys left, New Orleans was like a clearing house. And they had many men that was recruited out of the alley. That went in. You want me to go back to Pierron and AJ Pierron and Shaving Like My Sister Kate? Mm-hmm. And what happened there? Well, let me tell you the beginning then because I'm repeating some of this stuff. When we were at Rising Web and we were the big hit, Pierron sent to me a bundle of music to try to play for me. This is before Williams had joined his family. And amongst them was Sister Kate and I wish I could shimmy like my, no, I wish Mama's Baby Boy and Brown Skin Who You For, which they laid a place and with Will Ross of Chicago. This arrangement that we made on Sister Kate became famous around New York. Everybody wanted Sister Kate because it was a good number for them to play and fit in good jazz. Now you asked me about what kind of music Pierron played. Well, he played the same as any other band that played from notes. I see no difference in the music that he played and what white men, that is white men were playing at the time. They were Robichaud's band. They played too. Now whether they played by fake or by notes, I cannot attest to that because I was not in the room. But to me, it didn't sound any different than the music that I heard white men play at the different dances that were given at the different picnic grounds and other places of their era.
